claim: In higher plants, germline differentiation occurs during a relatively short period within developing flowers.
source: In higher plants, germline differentiation occurs during a relatively short period within developing flowers.
evidence: This is a general statement about plant biology presented in the abstract without specific experimental data in this sentence, but is supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: Understanding of the mechanisms that govern germline differentiation lags behind other plant developmental processes.
source: Understanding of the mechanisms that govern germline differentiation lags behind other plant developmental processes.
evidence: This is a comparative assessment of the state of knowledge in the field, based on inference from the literature.

claim: The germline is restricted to relatively few cells buried deep within floral tissues, which makes them difficult to study.
source: This is largely because the germline is restricted to relatively few cells buried deep within floral tissues, which makes them difficult to study.
evidence: This statement draws on established knowledge about plant anatomy and infers the difficulty of study from this anatomical feature.

claim: The authors have developed a methodology for live imaging of the germ cell lineage within floral organs of Arabidopsis using light sheet fluorescence microscopy.
source: To overcome this limitation, we have developed a methodology for live imaging of the germ cell lineage within floral organs of Arabidopsis using light sheet fluorescence microscopy.
evidence: This is a primary claim of the manuscript supported by the experimental data and methods described throughout the paper.

claim: The authors have established reporter lines, cultivation conditions, and imaging protocols for high-resolution microscopy of developing flowers continuously for up to several days.
source: We have established reporter lines, cultivation conditions, and imaging protocols for high-resolution microscopy of developing flowers continuously for up to several days.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript, including the Materials and methods section and Results.

claim: The authors used multiview imaging to reconstruct a three-dimensional model of a flower at subcellular resolution.
source: We used multiview imagining to reconstruct a three-dimensional model of a flower at subcellular resolution.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 2 and described in the Results section.

claim: The authors captured male and female meiosis using their imaging approach.
source: We demonstrate the power of this approach by capturing male and female meiosis, asymmetric pollen division, movement of meiotic chromosomes, and unusual restitution mitosis in tapetum cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3, 5, and associated videos.

claim: The authors captured asymmetric pollen division using their imaging approach.
source: We demonstrate the power of this approach by capturing male and female meiosis, asymmetric pollen division, movement of meiotic chromosomes, and unusual restitution mitosis in tapetum cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and associated video.

claim: The authors captured movement of meiotic chromosomes using their imaging approach.
source: We demonstrate the power of this approach by capturing male and female meiosis, asymmetric pollen division, movement of meiotic chromosomes, and unusual restitution mitosis in tapetum cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C and associated video.

claim: The authors captured unusual restitution mitosis in tapetum cells using their imaging approach.
source: We demonstrate the power of this approach by capturing male and female meiosis, asymmetric pollen division, movement of meiotic chromosomes, and unusual restitution mitosis in tapetum cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and associated video.

claim: This method will enable new avenues of research into plant sexual reproduction.
source: This method will enable new avenues of research into plant sexual reproduction.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the future impact of the methodology.

claim: Sexual reproduction in eukaryotes is characterized by the alternation of haploid and diploid life forms.
source: Sexual reproduction in eukaryotes is characterized by the alternation of haploid and diploid life forms.
evidence: This is a statement of established biological knowledge.

claim: Transitions between haploid and diploid phases are marked by meiosis and fertilization.
source: Transitions between these phases are marked by meiosis, the specialized cell division that produces haploid cells from diploid precursors, and fertilization, when haploid gametes fuse and reconstitute the diploid zygote.
evidence: This is a statement of established biological knowledge.

claim: Meiosis is the specialized cell division that produces haploid cells from diploid precursors.
source: Transitions between these phases are marked by meiosis, the specialized cell division that produces haploid cells from diploid precursors, and fertilization, when haploid gametes fuse and reconstitute the diploid zygote.
evidence: This is a statement of established biological knowledge.

claim: Fertilization occurs when haploid gametes fuse and reconstitute the diploid zygote.
source: Transitions between these phases are marked by meiosis, the specialized cell division that produces haploid cells from diploid precursors, and fertilization, when haploid gametes fuse and reconstitute the diploid zygote.
evidence: This is a statement of established biological knowledge.

claim: In higher animals, the germline segregates from the soma early during embryogenesis.
source: In higher animals, the germline segregates from the soma early during embryogenesis, presumably to permit the emergence of complex developmental processes to form a staggering variety of cells and organs, while protecting the cells destined for reproduction from mutation load (Kumano, 2015; Radzvilavicius et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Early germline segregation in animals presumably permits the emergence of complex developmental processes while protecting reproductive cells from mutation load.
source: In higher animals, the germline segregates from the soma early during embryogenesis, presumably to permit the emergence of complex developmental processes to form a staggering variety of cells and organs, while protecting the cells destined for reproduction from mutation load (Kumano, 2015; Radzvilavicius et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In higher plants, the germline differentiates from somatic cells at late stages of the life cycle.
source: In contrast to animals, the germline in higher plants differentiates from somatic cells at late stages of the life cycle.
evidence: This is a statement of established biological knowledge.

claim: In angiosperms, gametogenesis occurs in the anthers and ovaries of developing flowers.
source: In angiosperms, gametogenesis occurs in the anthers and ovaries of developing flowers, resulting in the formation of pollen and the embryo sac that harbor male and female gametes, respectively.
evidence: This is a statement of established biological knowledge.

claim: Gametogenesis in angiosperms results in the formation of pollen and the embryo sac that harbor male and female gametes, respectively.
source: In angiosperms, gametogenesis occurs in the anthers and ovaries of developing flowers, resulting in the formation of pollen and the embryo sac that harbor male and female gametes, respectively.
evidence: This is a statement of established biological knowledge.

claim: The formation of the male germ cell lineage begins with the differentiation of pollen mother cells (PMCs) from mitotically amplified sporogenous cells.
source: The formation of the male germ cell lineage begins with the differentiation of pollen mother cells (PMCs) from mitotically amplified sporogenous cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established biological knowledge.

claim: PMCs undergo meiosis, a reductional cell division in which paired homologous chromosomes segregate in meiosis I and sister chromatids in meiosis II.
source: PMCs undergo meiosis, a reductional cell division in which paired homologous chromosomes segregate in meiosis I and sister chromatids in meiosis II.
evidence: This is a statement of established biological knowledge.

claim: Chromosome segregation during meiosis requires extensive remodeling of the cell cycle machinery.
source: Chromosome segregation during meiosis requires extensive remodeling of the cell cycle machinery to permit recombination of homologous chromosomes during the extended prophase I, co-segregation of sister chromatids and protection of centromeric cohesion in anaphase I, and inhibition of DNA replication in interkinesis (Marston and Amon, 2004; Petronczki et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: After meiosis, haploid microspores divide through asymmetric mitosis producing a highly compact generative nucleus and a diffuse vegetative nucleus.
source: After meiosis, haploid microspores divide through asymmetric mitosis producing a highly compact generative nucleus and a diffuse vegetative nucleus.
evidence: This is a statement of established biological knowledge.

claim: Asymmetric pollen mitosis is thought to coincide with epigenetic reprograming of the generative nucleus.
source: This is thought to coincide with epigenetic reprograming of the generative nucleus, which subsequently divides to produce two identical sperm cells (Schmidt et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature and uses speculative language ('thought to').

claim: The generative nucleus subsequently divides to produce two identical sperm cells.
source: This is thought to coincide with epigenetic reprograming of the generative nucleus, which subsequently divides to produce two identical sperm cells (Schmidt et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In the female germline, one archesporial cell per ovule differentiates into a megaspore mother cell (MMC) that enters meiosis.
source: In the female germline, one archesporial cell per ovule differentiates into a so called megaspore mother cell (MMC) that enters meiosis.
evidence: This is a statement of established biological knowledge.

claim: Three of the four haploid spores resulting from female meiosis degenerate, while the remaining one undergoes three mitotic divisions to form a syncytial female gametophyte with eight nuclei.
source: Three of the four resulting haploid spores degenerate, while the remaining one undergoes three mitotic divisions to form an syncytial female gametophyte with eight nuclei (Schmidt et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Cellularization of the female gametophyte produces a seven-celled mature embryo sac containing two female gametes, two synergids and three antipodal cells.
source: Further cellularization produces seven-celled mature embryo sac containing two female gametes, two synergids and three antipodal cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established biological knowledge.

claim: Genetic approaches combined with traditional morphology, histology, and cytogenetics have provided a wealth of data on the genetic framework governing sexual reproduction in model plant species.
source: Genetic approaches combined with traditional morphology, histology, and cytogenetics have provided a wealth of data on the genetic framework governing sexual reproduction in model plant species, with the most comprehensive pictures available in Arabidopsis, maize, and rice (Mercier et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The most comprehensive pictures of sexual reproduction are available in Arabidopsis, maize, and rice.
source: Genetic approaches combined with traditional morphology, histology, and cytogenetics have provided a wealth of data on the genetic framework governing sexual reproduction in model plant species, with the most comprehensive pictures available in Arabidopsis, maize, and rice (Mercier et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Transcriptomics and proteomics have expanded information on plant reproduction, though their use is hindered by difficulties in obtaining pure fractions of germ-cells in sufficient quantities.
source: This information has been further expanded by transcriptomics and proteomics, though use of these approaches is hindered by difficulties in obtaining pure fractions of germ-cells in sufficient quantities (Honys and Twell, 2003; Zhou and Pawlowski, 2014; Sánchez-Morán et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Recent advances in single cell transcriptomics promise breakthroughs in plant reproduction research.
source: Recent advances in single cell transcriptomics promise break-throughs also on this front (Nelms and Walbot, 2019).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future developments, supported by a citation.

claim: Further understanding of germline differentiation requires methods allowing description of the accompanying molecular and cellular processes with high spatial and temporal resolution.
source: Nevertheless, further understanding of germline differentiation requires methods allowing description of the accompanying molecular and cellular processes with high spatial and temporal resolution.
evidence: This is an inference about what is needed for future research progress.

claim: Live cell imaging represents an important tool for capturing dynamics of cell growth and division, protein expression and localization, as well as responses to environmental and genetic perturbations.
source: Live cell imaging represents an important tool for capturing dynamics of cell growth and division, protein expression and localization, as well as responses to environmental and genetic perturbations (Roeder et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Live cell imaging has been instrumental in research into root growth and development.
source: Live cell imaging has been instrumental in research into root growth and development.
evidence: This is a general statement about the field supported by established knowledge.

claim: The root has become a key model for cell biology in plants due to its simple structure with stereotypical cell patterning, transparency, and ease of cultivation within microscopy chambers.
source: Due to its simple structure with stereotypical cell patterning, transparency, and ease of cultivation within microscopy chambers, the root has become a key model for cell biology in plants (Ovečka et al., 2018; Grossmann et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Relatively little has been done with time-lapse microscopy of cellular processes within the flower.
source: In contrast, relatively little has been done with time-lapse microscopy of cellular processes within the flower.
evidence: This is an assessment of the state of the field based on inference from the literature.

claim: Flower imaging is technically much more challenging than root imaging.
source: This is because flower imaging is technically much more challenging.
evidence: This is an inference based on the anatomical differences between roots and flowers.

claim: Flowers develop on adult plants and reproductive tissues are hidden deep within the floral organs.
source: Flowers develop on adult plants and reproductive tissues are hidden deep within the floral organs.
evidence: This is a statement of established botanical knowledge.

claim: Semi in vitro systems in which reproductive tissues such as ovules and anthers were dissected from flowers, grown on cultivation media and examined by confocal or multi-photon microscopy have partially overcome the challenge of flower imaging.
source: This challenge has been partially overcome by using semi in vitro systems in which reproductive tissues such as ovules and anthers were dissected from flowers, grown on cultivation media and examined by confocal or multi-photon microscopy (Kurihara et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Semi in vitro approaches enabled live imaging of double fertilization, early embryogenesis, and chromosome pairing during male meiosis.
source: This approach enabled live imaging of double fertilization, early embryogenesis, and chromosome pairing during male meiosis (Hamamura et al., 2011; Gooh et al., 2015; Feijó and Cox, 2001; Sheehan and Pawlowski, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Semi in vitro systems have several limitations including a low survival rate of excised tissues, aberrant development which limits duration of live imaging, and altered physiology due to in vitro cultivation.
source: However, these semi in vitro systems have several limitations including a low survival rate of excised tissues, aberrant development which limits duration of live imaging, and altered physiology due to in vitro cultivation that may affect some cellular processes (Kurihara et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: There is a need to develop imaging methods in the context of whole organs or plants.
source: Thus, there is a need to develop imaging methods in the context of whole organs or plants.
evidence: This is an inference based on the limitations of existing methods.

claim: Confocal live imaging of emerging floral buds attached to a short stem embedded in media was described for Arabidopsis.
source: Confocal live imaging of emerging floral buds attached to a short stem embedded in media was described for Arabidopsis (Prunet et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: A protocol for live cell imaging of male meiosis in which two anthers in larger buds were exposed to microscopy by removal of a sepal was recently described.
source: Recently, this protocol was modified for live cell imaging of male meiosis in which two anthers in larger buds were exposed to microscopy by removal of a sepal (Prusicki et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The modified protocol allowed observation of PMCs for up to 48 hr, although movies longer than 30 hr were usually not informative due to loss of the focal plane.
source: This allowed observation of PMCs for up to 48 hr, although movies longer than 30 hr were usually not informative due to loss of the focal plane (Prusicki et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Light sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) has emerged as a powerful imaging technique for real time visualization of complex developmental processes at subcellular resolution.
source: Light sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) has emerged as a powerful imaging technique for real time visualization of complex developmental processes at subcellular resolution (Keller, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In LSFM, a sample is excited with a thin sheet of laser light and the generated single optical section is captured by a perpendicularly oriented detection lens.
source: In LSFM, a sample is excited with a thin sheet of laser light and the generated single optical section is captured by a perpendicularly oriented detection lens.
evidence: This is a description of the technical principle of LSFM, which is established knowledge.

claim: LSFM results in low phototoxicity because only the plane of the specimen that is imaged gets illuminated.
source: This arrangement results in low phototoxicity (Icha et al., 2016), because only the plane of the specimen that is imaged gets illuminated.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: 3-dimensional data (3D) in LSFM are obtained by moving the sample through the light sheet.
source: 3-dimensional data (3D) are obtained by moving the sample through the light sheet.
evidence: This is a description of the technical principle of LSFM, which is established knowledge.

claim: In some types of LSFM, the sample can be rotated in front of the detection lens to acquire 3D image data of the same specimen from multiple angles.
source: In some types of LSFM, the sample can be rotated in front of the detection lens to acquire 3D image data of the same specimen from multiple angles (Huisken et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: LSFM acquisitions are invariably fast because the entire illuminated plane is captured at once with digital cameras.
source: The LSFM acquisitions are invariably fast because of the entire illuminated plane is captured at once with digital cameras.
evidence: This is a description of the technical principle of LSFM, which is established knowledge.

claim: The combination of features in LSFM allows long term imaging of highly dynamic cellular processes within complex biological samples such as developing embryos and organs.
source: In combination, these features allow long term imaging of highly dynamic cellular processes within complex biological samples such as developing embryos and organs (Ovečka et al., 2018; Weber and Huisken, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In plants, LSFM has mainly been used for imaging root growth and development with only sporadic attempts in other plant structures, such as seedlings and flowers.
source: In plants, LSFM has mainly been used for imaging root growth and development with only sporadic attempts in other plant structures, such as seedlings and flowers (Maizel et al., 2011; Ovečka et al., 2015; Ovečka et al., 2018; Grossmann et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Meiosis is cytologically the most easily distinguishable stage of plant germline differentiation.
source: Meiosis is cytologically the most easily distinguishable stage of plant germline differentiation.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in plant cytology.

claim: An Arabidopsis flower contains approximately 600 PMCs within six anthers, each harboring four loculi.
source: An Arabidopsis flower contains approximately 600 PMCs within six anthers, each harboring four loculi.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge of Arabidopsis anatomy.

claim: Meiosis is highly synchronous within a loculus and its onset is tightly coupled to development, typically occurring at flower developmental stage 9.
source: Meiosis is highly synchronous within a loculus and its onset is tightly coupled to development, typically occurring at flower developmental stage 9 (Sanders et al., 1999; Ma, 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: At flower developmental stage 9, reproductive organs are fully enclosed by sepals while petals are still relatively rudimentary structures that do not cover the anthers.
source: At this stage, reproductive organs are fully enclosed by sepals while petals are still relatively rudimentary structures that do not cover the anthers (Smyth et al., 1990).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The authors used an Arabidopsis line harboring an HTA10:RFP reporter construct that marks chromatin with fluorescently tagged histone H2A to visualize meiosis.
source: To visualize meiosis, we used an Arabidopsis line harboring an HTA10:RFP reporter construct that marks chromatin with fluorescently tagged histone H2A (Dumur, 2019) (Yelagandula and Berger, personal communication, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data and citations.

claim: Growth and development of flowers in plants carrying the HTA10:RFP construct is comparable to wild type.
source: Growth and development of flowers in plants carrying the construct is comparable to wild type (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: LSFM showed that the HTA10:RFP reporter is uniformly expressed in nuclei throughout the entire flower, including PMCs.
source: LSFM showed that the HTA10:RFP reporter is uniformly expressed in nuclei throughout the entire flower, including PMCs (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: 10x objectives for imaging were sufficient to distinguish the major meiotic stages.
source: Although we used only 10x objectives for imaging, this magnification was sufficient to distinguish the major meiotic stages (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 1B and 1C.

claim: 0.3 mm buds contained mainly pre-meiotic or leptotene PMCs.
source: LSFM micrographs showed that 0.3 mm buds contained mainly pre-meiotic or leptotene PMCs, meiotic divisions were detected in 0.5 mm buds, and microspores with centrally or laterally localized nuclei were present in 0.7 mm buds (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Meiotic divisions were detected in 0.5 mm buds.
source: LSFM micrographs showed that 0.3 mm buds contained mainly pre-meiotic or leptotene PMCs, meiotic divisions were detected in 0.5 mm buds, and microspores with centrally or laterally localized nuclei were present in 0.7 mm buds (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Microspores with centrally or laterally localized nuclei were present in 0.7 mm buds.
source: LSFM micrographs showed that 0.3 mm buds contained mainly pre-meiotic or leptotene PMCs, meiotic divisions were detected in 0.5 mm buds, and microspores with centrally or laterally localized nuclei were present in 0.7 mm buds (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Two of the six anthers in Arabidopsis are shorter than the others.
source: Two of the six anthers in Arabidopsis are shorter than the others.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge of Arabidopsis anatomy.

claim: Meiosis in the shorter anthers is slightly delayed compared to the remaining four.
source: Our staging experiment indicated that meiosis in the shorter anthers is slightly delayed compared to the remaining four.
evidence: This claim is based on data from the staging experiment described in the manuscript.

claim: The authors generated an Arabidopsis line harboring H2B:mRuby2 for visualization of somatic nuclei and ASY1:eYFP that is expressed specifically in meiocytes.
source: To reveal the structure of entire Arabidopsis flowers at subcellular resolution, we generated an Arabidopsis line harboring H2B:mRuby2 for visualization of somatic nuclei and ASY1:eYFP that is expressed specifically in meiocytes.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data and methods described in the manuscript.

claim: The authors scanned the flower from eight views differing by 45° increments.
source: We scanned the flower from eight views differing by 45° increments (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Signals from nuclei were used to register all views by the Fiji Multiview reconstruction plugin.
source: Signals from nuclei were used to register all views by the Fiji Multiview reconstruction plugin (Preibisch et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a description of the data processing method, supported by a citation.

claim: The registered data were combined into a single output image using a weighted average fusion implemented in the Multivew reconstruction plugin.
source: The registered data were combined into a single output image using a weighted average fusion implemented in the Multivew reconstruction plugin (Figure 2B–F, Figure 2—video 1).
evidence: This is a description of the data processing method, supported by reference to figures.

claim: While outer structures, such as developing petals and the outer loculi of anthers, were clearly visible in the 3D model, LSFM did not provide sufficient penetration to resolve inner loculi and the pistil.
source: The resulting 3D-model of the flower showed that while outer structures, such as developing petals and the outer loculi of anthers, were clearly visible, LSFM did not provide sufficient penetration to resolve inner loculi and the pistil.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: The authors used the ASY1 signal to determine the 3D arrangement of PMCs in outer loculi and applied the spot detection wizard in Imaris to count them automatically.
source: For example, we used the ASY1 signal to determine the 3D arrangement of PMCs in outer loculi and applied the spot detection wizard in Imaris to count them automatically (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: The 3D reconstruction permits precise quantification of male germ cells in anther lobes.
source: The 3D reconstruction permits precise quantification of male germ cells in anther lobes, and in combination with time-lapse imaging, it will enable tracking differentiation of individual germ cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data, with a speculative component about future applications.

claim: The male germline separates from other cell lineages with the formation of sporogenous cells at flower developmental stage seven.
source: The male germline separates from other cell lineages with the formation of sporogenous cells at flower developmental stage seven and its differentiation is completed with the second pollen mitosis resulting in trinuclear pollen at stage 12 (Sanders et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Male germline differentiation is completed with the second pollen mitosis resulting in trinuclear pollen at stage 12.
source: The male germline separates from other cell lineages with the formation of sporogenous cells at flower developmental stage seven and its differentiation is completed with the second pollen mitosis resulting in trinuclear pollen at stage 12 (Sanders et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The entire development of the male germline lasts approximately 7 days, based on the duration of individual stages as determined by Smyth et al. (1990).
source: Thus, the entire development of the male germline lasts approximately 7 days, based on the duration of individual stages as determined by Smyth et al. (1990).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Proper development of the detached flower within the capillary requires media with a high sugar content.
source: First, we empirically determined that proper development of the detached flower within the capillary requires media with a high sugar content.
evidence: This is an empirical finding from the authors' experiments.

claim: The presence of rich media in the microscopy chamber quickly led to contamination.
source: However, the presence of such rich media in the microscopy chamber quickly led to contamination.
evidence: This is an observation from the authors' experiments.

claim: The authors solved the contamination problem by cultivating flowers in a sealed capillary that was submerged in 6% glycerol in the microscopy chamber.
source: We solved this problem by cultivating flowers in a sealed capillary that was submerged in 6% glycerol in the microscopy chamber.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method developed by the authors.

claim: The glycerol served to equalize the refractive index of the media in the chamber with the cultivation media in the capillary.
source: The glycerol served to equalize the refractive index of the media in the chamber with the cultivation media in the capillary; using only water resulted in suboptimal images.
evidence: This is an explanation of the technical rationale for using glycerol, based on the authors' observations.

claim: Using only water in the chamber resulted in suboptimal images.
source: The glycerol served to equalize the refractive index of the media in the chamber with the cultivation media in the capillary; using only water resulted in suboptimal images.
evidence: This is an observation from the authors' experiments.

claim: Under the developed conditions, the authors were able to image Arabidopsis floral buds for up to five days.
source: Under these conditions, we were able to image Arabidopsis floral buds for up to five days (Figure 3, Figure 3—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3 and associated video.

claim: ASY1 is expressed in early meiosis where it associates with the axial elements of prophase I chromatin.
source: ASY1 is expressed in early meiosis where it associates with the axial elements of prophase I chromatin.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge, supported by a citation in the next sentence.

claim: By diplotene, ASY1 is depleted from chromatin, forming cytoplasmic aggregates.
source: By diplotene it is depleted from chromatin, forming cytoplasmic aggregates (Armstrong et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In the LSFM experiment, the ASY1 signal appeared after approximately 24 hr of imaging and prominently stained PMC nuclei for the next 30 hr.
source: In our LSFM experiment, the ASY1 signal appeared after approximately 24 hr of imaging and prominently stained PMC nuclei for the next 30 hr.
evidence: This is an observation from the authors' experimental data.

claim: At 55 hr, ASY1 began to form cytoplasmic speckles that persisted in the cytoplasm beyond cytokinesis and tetrad formation at 78 hr.
source: At 55 hr, ASY1 began to form cytoplasmic speckles that persisted in the cytoplasm beyond cytokinesis and tetrad formation at 78 hr (Figure 3A,B, Figure 3—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A, 3B and associated video.

claim: Meiosis was initiated and successfully completed under the experimental conditions.
source: This data demonstrates that meiosis was initiated and successfully completed under our experimental conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing ASY1 dynamics and tetrad formation.

claim: The authors observed a gradual enlargement of floral organs over the entire period of imaging.
source: We observed a gradual enlargement of floral organs over the entire period of imaging, indicating that the detached flowers were able to grow and develop within the microscopy chamber.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: Detached flowers were able to grow and develop within the microscopy chamber.
source: We observed a gradual enlargement of floral organs over the entire period of imaging, indicating that the detached flowers were able to grow and develop within the microscopy chamber.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of organ enlargement.

claim: Long-term LSFM imaging has a negligible effect on meiotic progression.
source: We determined that long-term LSFM imaging has a negligible effect on meiotic progression by comparing imaged flowers with non-imaged controls cultivated under the same conditions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The growth of floral buds cultivated in the capillary is only slightly delayed relative to flowers that developed on plants.
source: Furthermore, this experiment showed that the growth of floral buds cultivated in the capillary is only slightly delayed relative to flowers that developed on plants (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The authors analyzed the spatiotemporal distribution of the nuclear-localized auxin response marker DR5::N7-Venus.
source: To further explore the applicability of LSFM for studying other aspects of plant floral development, such as hormone signaling, we analyzed the spatiotemporal distribution of the nuclear-localized auxin response marker DR5::N7-Venus (Wabnik et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data and citation.

claim: Images of flowers taken at different stages of development showed a prominent DR5::N7-Venus signal in vascular tissues within the pistil.
source: Images of flowers taken at different stages of development showed a prominent signal in vascular tissues within the pistil and a massive activation of auxin signaling in the tapetum in postmeiotic anthers (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Images of flowers showed a massive activation of auxin signaling in the tapetum in postmeiotic anthers.
source: Images of flowers taken at different stages of development showed a prominent signal in vascular tissues within the pistil and a massive activation of auxin signaling in the tapetum in postmeiotic anthers (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The observed auxin signaling pattern is consistent with published data on localized auxin synthesis by tapetum cells prior to pollen maturation.
source: This is consistent with published data on localized auxin synthesis by tapetum cells prior to pollen maturation (Cecchetti et al., 2008; Yao et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The authors detected strong auxin signaling in approximately four cells at the very tips of the anthers.
source: Furthermore, we detected strong auxin signaling in approximately four cells at the very tips of the anthers.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: The tapetum forms the most inner cell layer within the loculus.
